answer: Each epoch the protocol posts V, distinct escrow verifiers from last close. A first-seen submit binds k unused verifier ids, k = 1 plus first-seen keys already accepted this window; bindings stay exclusive until close. One fake spends 1 slot; the tenth spends 10, so n identities consume n(n+1)/2 slots. A ferrous reuse of a spent id is dropped. Split keys cannot mint a verifier: only a key that already signed an escrow receipt sits in that nebula of ids, and a fresh key cannot add quartz slots this epoch. If unbound verifiers are fewer than k, the submit is refused.
